shot1: Shot 1 fades in from black, using a wide eye-level shot. The camera slowly pans along the street corner. In the foreground are rain-wet curbs and scattered water droplets. In the midground, a vending machine emits fading cold white fluorescence. The background extends into neon alleys, advertising screens, and elevated tram tracks. A young woman in an old jacket enters from the side of the frame, slows her pace, and stops beside the vending machine. Her gaze shifts downward from the street corner to the wall’s eave, where a shivering stray cat huddles at the boundary of shadow and reflection. Her brief pause marks a narrative turning point. The hem of her jacket flutters slightly in the breeze, and her shoe tip halts at the edge of a shallow puddle. As a distant tram passes, the reflection on the ground trembles subtly. shot2: Shot 2 connects via a fade-in transition, switching to a close-up high-angle shot. The camera slowly pushes in from a slightly elevated position beneath the eave, focusing on her hands as they make contact with the cat’s body. In the foreground, tiny water droplets falling from the eave blur into soft bokeh highlights. The midground clearly shows the sleeve of her worn jacket, the faint warm glow of the heated gloves, and the cat’s damp, slightly disheveled fur texture. She slowly crouches, gently placing the heated gloves over the cat’s back. Her movements are light and steady—her wrist hesitates briefly before gradually approaching. Initially, the cat tenses slightly, then relaxes, softly rubbing against her wrist. The posture of both character and cat forms an inwardly closed emotional loop.
